review_conclusions: The planning gate is relaxed only for Query nodes carrying a compiled typed-operation closure.
TypeScript and Python bindings consume operation, property, and Rule records from that compiled closure; authored source changes therefore change closure identity and generated bytes.
Rust retains the established typed-operation lowering and adds a Query-specific alias to the same closure digest.
The three language bindings fail on missing inputs or unresolved properties and do not introduce ambient default or truthiness semantics.
Operation and Rule paths remain regression-clean in the 119-test aggregate suite.
residual_risks: The B05 runtime corpus directly exercises the selected Query's all/not/eq guard; broader typed operators remain covered by compiler validation and the established Rule/Rust suites rather than a separate Query corpus.
B05 does not establish Calculation, Mapping, Policy, whole-project atomicity, or L1 aggregate completion.
reviewer_independence: The parent did not author the three helper-owned binding files and independently inspected their exact diff and reran aggregate validation.
